blind_spots_patched: Omitted the $11.76B 2027-2030 debt maturity wall (51.2% of YE2025 debt), 2026 gross debt expansion (+$1.14B to $24.138B at Q3 plus $1.2B Nov 17 5.800% 2037 notes), -$523M working-capital deficit (0.90x current ratio), CQP VIE ring-fencing ($14.395B / 60.2% of net debt and $569M cash inside 48.6%-owned CQP), 1.25x DSCR subsidiary distribution covenants, declining capitalized interest (+17.8% net interest expense), and $2.9B Midscale 8&9 EPC commitments.

Missed the 112.5% YoY Q3 surge in short-term CMI marketing volumes (119 TBtu vs 56 TBtu; 9M 352 TBtu vs 203 TBtu) and 73% variable revenue share occurring during a Strait of Hormuz-driven TTF/JKM price spike (~$28.5/MMBtu in Oct 2026) that management warns may not recur, plus the June 2026 NPNS reclassification embedding non-cash basis amortization into future COGS.

Understated the 2026-2028 competing Gulf Coast and global LNG supply wave beyond Plaquemines Phase 1: Venture Global CP2 Phase 2 March 2026 FID ($8.6B financing, 29.0 mtpa contracted post-COD, D.C. Circuit win, 8 owned tankers), Plaquemines 27.2 mtpa Non-FTA authorization, ExxonMobil/QatarEnergy Golden Pass LNG Train 1-2 ramp, and EIA's forecast of U.S. exports surging 25.8% from 15.1 to 19.0 Bcf/d (2025-2027).

Missed the Nov 16, 2026 promotion of CFO Zach Davis to President & CFO across both Cheniere Energy, Inc. and Cheniere Partners GP (concentrating operational and financial authority), routine Nov 2026 Form 4 filings (no open-market insider sales), and the tension between an expanded $10B 2026-2030 buyback authorization ($8.4B remaining) + >12% Q3 dividend hike vs. rising consolidated gross debt.

Omitted the USTR April 2025 Section 301 maritime mandate requiring 1% of U.S. LNG exports to move on U.S.-built vessels beginning April 2029 and escalating to 15% by April 2047 (unmodified despite Nov 2025 one-year deferral of China-linked vessel fees), alongside retaliatory tariff exposure in importing markets.
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: No external customer contributed 10% or more of consolidated external-customer revenue (based on FY2025 10-K diversification baseline).
WEAKENED: Consolidated debt stood near $22.8 billion at year-end 2025 and Cheniere repaid $307 million of consolidated long-term debt in 9M 2026.
WEAKENED: Long-term Integrated Production Marketing (IPM) agreements remain marked to market through GAAP cost of sales prior to physical delivery, driving large recurring derivative swings.

CONFIRMED: CCL Stage 3 reached substantial completion on August 28, 2026 ahead of schedule and within budget, CCL Midscale 8&9 was 58.6% complete at Q3 2026, and SPL Expansion Phase 1 remained conditional on permits and FID.
